In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of Ca(2+ )dependent inactivation of L-type Ca2 + channel.

the molecular mechanisms of the Ca2+ channel regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca(2+)/CaM binding to the cytoplasmatic region of the alpha subunit is required for Ca(2+) dependent inactivation.
Ca(2+), through its binding to the alpha 1 cytoplasmic domain, modulates the channel in a manner that is dependent on the ion selectivity of the channel.
Ca(2+)/calmodulin binds to a site on the cytoplasmically oriented segment of the cardiac L-type alpha 1 subunits and that this binding results in the inactivation of Ca2+ current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction between the alpha 1 and beta subunits and a specific region of the alpha subunit are important for Ca(2+) dependent inactivation of cardiac Ca2+ channels.
Ca(2+), which is the primary activator of cardiac L-type calcium channel, also serves to terminate its own action.
